question: As the Commission is well aware, the SAMCA Group project for the Doade lithium mine was initially cancelled by the High Court of Justice of Galicia, as a result of the project’s irregularities and negative environmental impact. One of the Commission experts who assessed the 47 strategic projects was the director of the failed SAMCA Group project in Doade before becoming a Commission expert for the 47 projects.
He is now director of mining at Recursos de Galicia (RDG), the public-private company that manages the mine’s operations. In light of the above: 1.

Does the Commission not believe that a Commission expert’s participation in the failed project, selection and now implementation of the Doade lithium mine strategic project taints the process and generates a questionable conflict of interest – which Galician courts have already warned about?
Will the Commission take into account this conflict of interest, which tarnishes the Doade mine strategic project and should therefore entail removal of the ‘strategic project’ seal?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (21.10.2025) The Commission assesses applications submitted to the call for Strategic Projects under the Critical Raw Materials Act1 (CRMA) with the help of external experts. These experts are selected from the Commission’s experts database, established following an open call for expressions of interest.

The Commission stresses that the Mina Doade application has been assessed by experts without conflicts of interest. None of these experts were director of the SAMCA Group or were involved in companies managing the mine’s operations, as this would have clearly constituted a conflict of interest.

Each application is assessed by at least four individual experts whose collective expertise covers technical, financial, and environmental, social and governance-related aspects, as well as the United Nations Framework Classification for Resources.

When allocating experts to applications, the Commission pays particular attention to the impartiality of the involved experts and to avoiding any potential conflicts of interest. For instance, before receiving access to the application, experts have to confirm in writing the absence of conflicts of interests with the applications allocated to them.
